sections.title: The space and what we assumed
sections.body: The city vacancy record gives the address and the last use, not the floor size. We size the room from the lot record where there is one (retail area ÷ storefronts on the lot), otherwise from a 20 × 40 ft default. Until someone tapes the walls it is an estimate, so the frontage and depth carry a margin and every check below is tested at the worst end of it.

sections.title: Getting in and through
sections.body: The entrance sits at 62% of the frontage. A 1.2 m aisle runs straight from the door to the counter, and the window bar stops short of the door to leave the 60 in turning space.

sections.title: Counter and queue
sections.body: The back of house takes 2.1 m off the back wall. The counter stands in front of it, set off the left wall, with a staff pass at the right end. Both move with the walls, which is why two of these checks carry the full wall margin.

sections.title: Seating: 14 seats
sections.body: Stools face the street at the window bar. Two-tops fill the floor between the bar and the queue, each with a 36 in route around it.

sections.title: Furniture and equipment: 31 items
sections.body: Click any item in the model for its product page. Only the sofa and the pendants are the exact modeled products; the rest link to one comparable product each.

sections.title: How the agent built this
steps: Read the space: 23 ft wide × 47 ft deep, about 1081 sq ft (100 m²)
Read the brief: 12 seats, mostly dine-in, window bar, sofa lounge
Back of house: fridge, three-compartment sink and shelving along the back wall, 2.1 m deep
Counter: 4 × 1.2 m modules with espresso machine and pastry case, a 0.915 m staff pass on the right, 3 pendants above
Queue: 1.5 m kept clear in front of the counter
Main aisle: a straight 1.2 m path from the door to the counter
Window bar: 7 stools facing the street, with a 0.915 m aisle behind them
Lounge: velvet sofa, coffee table and armchair on the left wall (+3 seats)
Banquette: a 2.6 m bench on the left wall with 2 small tables and a chair opposite each (+4 seats), keeping the middle free to walk
Tables: 2 two-tops, with at least 0.915 m of accessible route between groups
Checks: 4/4 passed
